sentences.text: Pahasapasaurus is distinguished by its elongated epipodial bones in the forelimbs and hindlimbs and by the specific structure of its palate bones.
The genus name Pahasapasaurus is derived from the Sioux language, meaning "Black Hills".
The specific name haasi honors Charles Christian Haas, the discoverer of the fossil.
Bruce Schumacher formally named the species Pahasapasaurus haasi in 2007 based on a partial skeleton with a skull and lower jaws.
Pahasapasaurus belongs to the family Polycotylidae.
The type species Pahasapasaurus haasi lived during the late Cenomanian age in the Greenhorn Limestone of South Dakota.
A second species, Pahasapasaurus gillettei, lived during the early Turonian age in the Tropic Shale of Utah.
Pahasapasaurus lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
